question: Is all discoverable Indus evidence indexed with its available metadata, and what would a complete index require?
outcome: 123 contributing rows join to 115 site/provenance entities and represent 5652 of 5680 local faces. Across 19 CISI 1 ranges, 327 of 493 base identifiers match locally and 166 do not. Of 114 museum originals, 61 have confirmed identifier joins and 53 remain unjoined. A purposive 20-site source sample has 14 supported and six qualified assertions. Worldwide missing physical objects and recall remain unknown.
challenge: Overlapping site labels, mixed catalogue classes, historical versus current inventories, face versus object units, inaccessible complete catalogues and incomplete source/asset metadata prevent a global denominator.
remedy: Preserve source-specific count assertions and candidate identities; use source-attested aliases and concordances; normalize metadata placeholders; inspect selected primary witnesses; propose inventory dispositions, schema extensions and a stratified 200-object pilot.
retry_when: Independent review identifies a correction, or current ICIT/full CISI/holding inventories, new registration concordances or original context/rights records become available. Recompute only in a new dated endpoint with the changed input or method recorded.
